title: BEVSA: A Real-Time Bird's-Eye-View Semantic Segmentation Accelerator for Multi-Camera System
problem: Bird's-eye-view (BEV) semantic segmentation for multi-camera systems (MCS) requires expensive view transformation (68.3 ms on edge devices) and exhibits high input activation sparsity (69.1%), resulting in low throughput and high latency unsuitable for real-time 3D perception.
motivation: Real-time BEV semantic segmentation is critical for autonomous driving and 3D scene understanding on edge devices, but computational bottlenecks prevent deployment.
method: BEVSA is a specialized hardware accelerator with two key innovations: (1) block-decomposed hierarchical BEV pooling that partitions search space in MCS-suitable ways, achieving 43.2x speedup over edge computing for BEV transformation, and (2) coarse-to-fine-grained zero-skipping convolution that handles both channel-level and tile-level sparsity, improving convolution throughput 1.61x. Implemented at 28nm, it targets edge deployment.
key_novelty: Hardware acceleration of BEV pooling with hierarchical decomposition and adaptive sparsity-aware convolution for real-time multi-camera semantic segmentation.
contributions: Block-decomposed hierarchical BEV pooling cluster achieving 43.2x speedup
Coarse-to-fine-grained zero-skipping convolution with 1.61x throughput improvement
Real-time BEV segmentation at 23.1 fps on edge device
167.4x energy efficiency improvement over edge computing baseline
primary_theme: Hardware-efficient BEV semantic segmentation via pooling and sparsity optimization
